books.section: Topic 1.5 Labor, Slavery, and Caste in the Spanish Colonial System
The Early Colonial Era: Spain Colonizes the New World

primary_sources.work: New Laws of 1542 (Leyes Nuevas), royal reforms pushed by Bartolome de las Casas

parts.modelAnswer: The New Laws forbade new grants of Native labor under the encomienda. They also ordered existing grants to end when the holder died.
parts.prompt: Identify one reform the New Laws made.

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for naming one accurate reform, such as the ban on new grants, the end of grants at the holder's death, or the ban on Native enslavement.
scoring.notEarned: Naming the encomienda without a reform stated does not earn the point.

parts.modelAnswer: Las Casas campaigned against the cruelty of the encomienda, and his writings reached the Crown. The king issued the laws to curb the abuses and bring colonial labor under royal control.
parts.prompt: Explain why the Spanish Crown issued the New Laws.

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for explaining one accurate cause, such as Las Casas's campaign, reports of cruelty, or the Crown's wish to control the encomenderos.
scoring.notEarned: Stating only that the Crown wanted reform, with no cause given, does not earn the point.

parts.modelAnswer: Colonists in the Americas resisted fiercely, and enforcement across an ocean was weak. The demand for coerced labor also survived, so Spain turned to enslaved Africans instead of ending forced labor.
parts.prompt: Explain one reason the New Laws had limited effect.

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for explaining one accurate reason for the limited effect, such as colonist resistance, weak enforcement, or the continued demand for coerced labor.
scoring.notEarned: Stating only that the laws failed, with no reason given, does not earn the point.

source: original; stimulus is a paraphrase of the New Laws of 1542 (public domain)

stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of the New Laws of 1542, the royal reforms pushed by Bartolome de las Casas.
stimulus.text: Paraphrase of the New Laws of 1542. The laws declared that Native peoples were free subjects of the Crown, not slaves. They forbade new grants of Native labor under the encomienda, ordered existing grants to end with the death of the holder, and banned the enslavement of Native peoples.
